scores.claim_text: BrightSpring operates over 180 pharmacies, infusion centers, and specialty oncology locations across all 50 states, and over 1,000 accredited pharmacies/branches/agencies/service locations (ACHC, CHAP, Joint Commission, CARF, NABP, URAC, DMEPOS).
scores.interpretation: Sector-registry mismatch: Drugs@FDA indexes NDA/ANDA drug-APPROVAL holders (manufacturers), not dispensing/infusion/specialty pharmacies. PharMerica/Amerita are dispensers, so 0 approvals is expected and NON-informative (not a contradiction). State pharmacy-board licenses and accreditation-body rosters (ACHC/Joint Commission) are the correct registry for a 180-pharmacy/1,000-location claim and are not in this catalog. The brand network is independently corroborated elsewhere (PharMerica = 110 EDGAR mentions; Onco360 = 11), so existence is not in doubt; the specific facility COUNT is simply not federally verifiable here. Scored UNVERIFIABLE honestly rather than forcing openFDA absence into severity.

scores.claim_text: Walgreen Co. (affiliate of Walgreens Boots Alliance) is a major shareholder (collectively with KKR ~67.9% voting power) and a related-party inventory supplier under which BrightSpring purchases a significant volume of inventory.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts 'BrightSpring' in WBA filings (cik 0001618921) + all-filer external validation
scores.M_value: WBA discloses 'BrightSpring' 12x in its own 10-Q/10-K filings (incl. 10-Q filed 2024-01-04, pre-cutoff); 72 total external-filer mentions
scores.interpretation: Direct counterparty corroboration. Walgreens Boots Alliance independently discloses BrightSpring in its own SEC filings 12 times, consistent with a material equity-method/related-party relationship. The shareholder + inventory-supplier claim is the kind a large counterparty WOULD disclose, and it does. Strong PASS.

scores.claim_text: BrightSpring is one of the leading independent specialty pharmacies in oncology in the U.S., operating the Onco360 specialty oncology pharmacy brand.
scores.M_value: Onco360 EDGAR FTS = 11 hits (AVEO Pharmaceuticals, Puma Biotechnology and other oncology drug manufacturers reference Onco360 as a specialty-pharmacy distribution partner); openFDA = 0 (expected for a dispenser)
scores.interpretation: Independent oncology drug manufacturers name Onco360 in their own 8-Ks/presentations as a specialty-pharmacy channel partner. That is exactly the external footprint a genuinely-operating leading independent oncology specialty pharmacy would leave. openFDA 0 is non-informative (dispenser, not approval-holder). Corroborated -> PASS. (The 'leading' superlative is subjective and not separately scored.)

scores.claim_text: BrightSpring published a peer-reviewed real-world-evidence study propensity-matching ~700 ExactCare patients to ~1,400 non-ExactCare Medicare Advantage members across eight states (2007-2018) showing improved outcomes/cost.
scores.interpretation: The claim describes a RETROSPECTIVE observational claims-database (real-world-evidence) study, not a prospective interventional trial. Retrospective insurer-database analyses are generally NOT registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, so absence is expected and non-contradicting. No federal registry covers a peer-reviewed RWE publication. Scored UNVERIFIABLE per calibration (do not manufacture severity from a registry that does not cover the claim type).

scores.claim_text: Diversified payor mix (Dec 31, 2022): 48% Medicare (35% Part D), 23% Medicaid, 19% Commercial, 4% government, 6% private/other -- majority of revenue reimbursed by CMS/Medicare/Medicaid.
scores.M_value: 4 UEIs resolved; 6 contracts totaling ~$2.97M (PharMerica pharmacy services for AFRH/Treasury + DoD); 0 grants
scores.interpretation: Medicare/Medicaid REIMBURSEMENT flows through CMS claims-adjudication systems, NOT USAspending contract/grant data, so USAspending structurally cannot confirm a payor-mix %. The query does confirm the entities are real federally-registered recipients (real UEIs, small direct federal pharmacy contracts), which is a mild positive consistency check but does not ground-truth the 48/23 split. No catalog registry covers CMS reimbursement mix -> UNVERIFIABLE (honestly), not severity. (Small ~$3M direct federal contracts are immaterial vs $7.7B revenue and are not what the claim asserts.)

scores.claim_text: ~$3.4B long-term debt (First Lien tranches + $450M Second Lien) with 2026-2027 balloon maturities and a springing-maturity covenant; in compliance with all financial covenants; KKR/WBA 1%-of-EBITDA monitoring fee.
scores.M_check: going_concern_detector(cik 0001865782) + ucc_proxy(cik 0001865782) + prospectus clean audit opinion
scores.M_value: going_concern signal = NO_GOING_CONCERN; ucc_proxy = LOW_LIEN_EXPOSURE (pre-IPO private filer, no 8-K 2.03 history); KPMG audit opinion in prospectus is unqualified
scores.interpretation: Heavy KKR-backed leverage is HONESTLY and fully disclosed in the prospectus (debt tranches, rates, balloon dates, covenant ratio 6.90x, springing maturity, related-party monitoring fee). The audit opinion is clean and there is no going-concern language. Under the honesty-alpha framework, fully-disclosed leverage with a clean audit and covenant compliance is a PASS -- the framework rewards honest disclosure of bad-ish facts rather than re-penalizing disclosed risk. No registry contradicts the disclosure. (NOTE: the going_concern connector returned a post-cutoff 2026 10-K; that post-cutoff content was disregarded per blinding discipline -- only the NO_GOING_CONCERN signal direction, consistent with the clean IPO-date audit, was used.)

scores.claim_text: PharMerica settled a False Claims Act / Anti-Kickback qui tam (Relator Silver, D.N.J.) for an estimated $115.0M in Nov 2023, without admitting liability, subject to DOJ/court approval; $115M accrued in SG&A.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts 'PharMerica' (all filers) + prospectus self-disclosure of accrued $115M settlement
scores.M_value: PharMerica = 110 EDGAR full-text mentions (well-established named entity); the prospectus itself books the $115M ($105M accrued current, $10M long-term) and discloses the FCA/AKS history transparently
scores.interpretation: This is a self-disclosed legal-settlement liability fully booked in the financials and described in detail (procedural history, settlement amount, accrual split). The framework's value here is that the issuer disclosed an adverse FCA/AKS matter honestly and reserved for it. No registry contradicts the disclosure; the entity is independently well-documented. Honest disclosure of a material negative -> PASS (not a hidden/inflated claim). The matter itself is a genuine regulatory negative but it is transparently disclosed and reserved, which is the disclosure behavior the framework scores positively.
